purpose: Bidirectional obligation ledger between the Isabelle abstract model of kernel version 2 and the final source of the native token, the ERC-3643 profile adapter, and the profile governor. Every row names one load-bearing abstract condition and the four pieces of evidence that connect it to the code: the exact source consumer, the positive activation test, a declared negative detector, and the compiled or downstream consumer. The negative is a killed consumer-removal mutation when one source consumer can be removed, otherwise a bounded behavioral negative whose scope the row states. scripts/verify-obligation-ledger-v3.mjs checks every anchor against the current tree and renders the Isabelle ledger theory, the summary, and the central closure record.

claimLadder.current: mapped implementation evidence; end-to-end refinement incomplete
claimLadder.currentMeaning: Every load-bearing abstract condition that this ledger names has a named source consumer in the final code, a test that exercises its positive branch, a declared negative detector, and a compiled or downstream consumer. When one source consumer can be removed, the negative is a mutation recorded as KILLED by the current receipt. When no single-consumer removal is meaningful, the row names a bounded behavioral negative and its scope. The ledger is the enumeration of the conditions the review identified; the completeness of that enumeration is not proved. The abstract model is machine-checked. The link between the compiled runtime and the abstract transition system (the locale assumption pinned_runtime_refinement.runtime_link) is not discharged, so no theorem states that the compiled runtime implements the model.
claimLadder.nextRung: end-to-end refinement complete: requires a machine-checked discharge of pinned_runtime_refinement.runtime_link for the exact runtime templates named in the generated bridge, replayed independently, before any Full or refinement-complete wording is used.

closure.statusMeaning: The ledger has no CURRENT-MANDATORY row. The rows NAT-E2E-01 and ADP-E2E-01 are SUCCESSOR-MANDATORY: they name the undischarged runtime link that separates the current claim from the next rung. The closure stays CONDITIONAL until those rows are CLOSED.

preservation.statement: Each abstract admissibility condition, success state, failure stutter, and receipt projection in TRUST_Transaction_Refinement, TRUST_Bound_Dependency_Assume_Guarantee, TRUST_Retrieve_Relation, and TRUST_Verified_Profile_Onboarding is carried by at least one CLOSED row whose source consumer is in the final code of the endpoint that implements it.
preservation.coverage: native: authorization, authority epoch, nonce and identifier freshness, dependency currency and rebind, shape rules, canonical calldata, case transition table, custody backing, dispositions, reversal relation, ordinary transfers, dependency assessment, receipts, failure stutter, route closure, retrieve projections. adapter: single immutable authority, seal epoch, freshness, dependency currency, shape and calldata, case table, custody confinement, import initial state, owned upstream state and resynchronisation, upstream dependency failures, receipts, route closure, seal. governor: canonical manifest and one-way seal.

reflection.statement: Every guard and state write on the typed command paths of the three endpoints is either the consumer of a row above or listed here as runtime-only with the reason it has no abstract counterpart. This direction is enumerated by review, not by a machine scan of the sources; the mechanical parts are that every consumer line a row cites exists with its declared occurrence count, that every declared fault of the mutation campaign is cited by a row or listed as campaign-only, and that every cited fault mutates a consumer file of its row. Selectors outside the generated route classification fall through the compiler dispatcher and revert with empty data (generic_dispatcher_selector_is_unclassified).

assumptions.statement: pinned_runtime_refinement.runtime_link: every accepted execution of the pinned runtime template corresponds to a concrete transaction whose abstraction is admitted by the model and reaches the expected success state or stutters. This is a locale assumption. Nothing in this ledger discharges it; the Kontrol proofs and the Foundry executions are bounded instances of it, not a proof of it.

solc 0.8.36 compiles the final source to the runtime templates named in the generated bridge correctly (compiler_correctness_remains_a_nonclaim). The deterministic build receipt establishes reproducibility, not correctness.
keccak-256 is collision resistant for the identifier, receipt hash, dependency root, nonce key, and case identifier preimages.
No deployed instance is bound. Deployment identity, immutable resolution, and chain context are outside this ledger.

Policy, identity, settlement, and entitlement dependencies (native) and the sealed token, Identity Registry, and Compliance (adapter) behave only through the typed boundary the model classifies (trust_external_assumptions, classify_dependency). Their internal correctness is not claimed.
CANCUN schedule semantics, in particular that a reverting call restores the whole state and emits no log, which the abstract failure stutters rely on (approved_evm_schedule).

The storage layout in the generated bridge is the compiler layout of the exact sources (sourceBinding); TRUST_State_Abi_Normal_Form proves label distinctness and nonaliasing over the declared finite preimages, not the compiler's implementation of the layout.
A KILLED mutation shows that the named detector depends on the named consumer; it does not show behavioral equivalence of the code and the model beyond the detector.

rows.title: A terminal case admits no further action
An overlay opens a fresh case or amends its own live head; it cannot enter another case
A second RESTRICT in its own case changes no state and is rejected
SEIZE requires a case that is not open; a disposition in an open overlay case is rejected
Every case opening advances the case generation
A disposition closes its case terminally
Terminality is scoped to one case; an overlay owned by another case stays live and its frozen target saturates at observation

consumerRemovalNegative.note: after a custody disposition in one case the test asserts that the freeze case of the same subject is still open with its head, that the frozen target reads as the saturated balance, and that UNFREEZE of that head is still admitted; removing the saturation or clearing the overlay on disposition fails the assertions

rows.title: FREEZE sets an absolute target that must strictly increase, pushes the live head, and records the prior target
RESTRICT sets the restriction flag and records the prior flag; freeze and restriction overlays are independent
SEIZE opens a custody case, moves the exact amount to the custodian, and records it as custody backing
Neither a transfer, a seizure, nor a direct disposition can spend custody backing or the own frozen floor
A custody disposition names the exact active custody record and consumes it
A disposition moves the exact amount between two accounts; CONFISCATE does not burn; total supply is preserved
LIQUIDATE binds the settlement pair as the receipt's external commitment
RECOVER consumes its entitlement commitment once
A reversal pairs only with the action kind it reverses
A reversal targets the subject's live head whose state still matches the original; a reversed action cannot be reversed again

consumerRemovalNegative.note: the existence guard on the effect record (the code consumer of the conjunct effect_links st action_id is not None) is masked for every reachable state by the applied-lifecycle check of the original record and by the live-head check of this row: an applied FREEZE or RESTRICT always has an effect record, and an unknown or reversed action fails the earlier checks with the same reason. Removing the guard alone is therefore not detectable by a test; the head-check mutation of this row removes the load-bearing condition.

rows.title: A terminal case admits no reversal
UNFREEZE restores the prior target, pops the head, and reopens the case on the parent or closes it
UNRESTRICT restores the prior flag and closes the case
RELEASE returns the exact active custody to the prior holder and closes the custody case
A successful reversal marks the original reversed and its receipt names the original as parent with the REVERSAL kind
An ordinary transfer respects the restriction flags of both parties
An ordinary transfer changes balances only and preserves every regulatory record

consumerRemovalNegative.note: the handler interleaves ordinary transfers with kernel commands and the invariants compare the frozen target, live head, and custody case against the handler's own model after every step; a transfer that touched any regulatory record would break the comparison

rows.title: A dependency response is applied only when canonical and echoed; a denial is a typed rejection; a malformed response is reason 202, an echo mismatch reason 203, a canonical operational failure reason 204
The identity dependency is assessed for every counterparty; dependency code or configuration drift is reason 200 or 201
The receipt is the keccak of its 17-word preimage, is stored under the command identifier, is returned, and is the final event of the transaction
The receipt binds the dependency root, the assessment evidence, and the ACTION kind of a forward command
Every rejection, operational failure, malformed input, and dependency revert is a persistent stutter: the state is unchanged and no receipt or event is committed

finalSourceConsumers.note: every failure path is a Solidity revert with a typed error; the EVM discards all state writes and logs of a reverting frame, which is the runtime realisation of the abstract stutter

consumerRemovalNegative.note: the test records the storage and log state before a rejected, an operationally failed, and a malformed call and asserts both are unchanged afterwards; every guard's own mutation additionally shows that removing the guard turns the stutter into a state change
